If sentiment is positive and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% to align with upward momentum.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% to reflect downward pressure.  
In mid-horizon (days 10–20), if sentiment is neutral and forecast deviates >1.5σ from 14-day moving average, adjust toward moving average.  
Late-horizon (days 20–30), if sentiment is mixed and forecast is trending flat, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.  
Early-horizon (days 1–10), if sentiment is positive and forecast is rising, add 0.5–1.0% upward momentum to reflect bullish sentiment.  
If sentiment spikes to 0.67+ and forecast is below 70.0, apply a 1.0–1.5% upward correction to capture sentiment-driven breakout.
